answer: Bonded escrows make each identity costly to operate, while correlated equivocation lets the protocol aggregate conflicts across a coordinated set: for k identities, pairwise evidence yields penalties scaling as O(k²), not merely k. Detection also triggers asymmetric capital depreciation, applying an exponential loss multiplier to the swarm’s collateral and making hidden coordination economically untenable. Like an orchard reflected in a mirror across the tundra, duplicated identities cannot safely conceal their shared behavior.
